overview.description: Gong Zhu (æ‹±çŒª - 'Chase the Pig' or 'Dig Out the Pig') is an enhanced Chinese version of Hearts. Penalty cards can be exposed before play to double (or quadruple) their effects. Features special roles for the Jack of Diamonds (sheep) and Ten of Clubs (transformer). Popular among Chinese Weiqi (Go) players between tournament games.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: China
Time Period: Late 20th century
Creator(s): Unknown (folk evolution from Hearts)
Etymology: 'Gong Zhu' (æ‹±çŒª) literally means 'to dig out/root out the pig' - the Queen of Spades is the 'pig' and players try to drive it out; the loser is called the pig and may have to grovel under the table
timeline: 19th Century: Hearts introduced to China through Western contact
Late 20th Century: Gong Zhu develops as a Chinese variation with exposing cards and special scoring
Modern Era: Popular among Chinese intellectuals, especially Weiqi (Go) players
Present Day: Played throughout China and in Chinese communities worldwide
history.evolution: Gong Zhu evolved from Western Hearts, adding the Chinese innovation of exposing cards to multiply their values, plus special scoring for the Jack of Diamonds (sheep) and Ten of Clubs (transformer). The game reflects Chinese preferences for gambling elements and dramatic swings in fortune.
history.cultural: Gong Zhu is particularly popular among Chinese Weiqi (Go) players, who play it to relax between tournament games. The game has a playful punishment tradition where the loser (the 'pig') may have to grovel under the table or wear a paper strip hanging from their mouth. The game represents the Chinese adaptation of Western card games with added complexity and gambling elements.

rules.objective: Avoid taking penalty cards (hearts and Queen of Spades). Collect the Jack of Diamonds for a bonus. The Ten of Clubs doubles all your scoring cards if you take any other scoring card, or scores +50 alone.
rules.gameplay:
1. Before play, players may expose certain cards to double their values
2. Holder of 2â™  leads first hand; thereafter, holder of Qâ™  (pig) from previous hand leads
3. Any card may be led (no restriction on hearts/spades)
4. Must follow suit if possible; may play any card if cannot follow
5. Highest card of led suit wins trick
6. Winner leads to next trick
keyRules: Four cards may be exposed before play: Aâ™¥, Qâ™ , Jâ™¦, 10â™£
Exposing doubles the card's value (or quadruples for 10â™£)
Exposed cards cannot be played first time their suit is led
No passing of cards (unlike Western Hearts)
Game ends when a player reaches -1000; that player is the 'pig'

strategy.basic:
For Beginners:
1. Avoid taking the Queen of Spades (pig) at all costs
2. Try to take the Jack of Diamonds (sheep) for positive points
3. Be careful with the Ten of Clubs - it can multiply your penalties
4. Consider exposing cards only if you have strong control of that suit
strategy.intermediate:
1. Track which hearts have been played
2. Decide whether to shoot for all hearts (+200) or avoid them
3. Use the exposing rule strategically - expose to double positive cards, or to protect yourself from being forced to take penalties
4. Lead suits where you have the exposed card to avoid playing it
strategy.advanced:
1. Calculate exact probabilities of who holds which cards
2. Bluff by exposing cards you don't need to protect
3. Coordinate with partner in partnership play
4. Read opponents' exposing decisions for information
5. Complex endgame decisions about whether to take all hearts
tips: Exposing the pig (Qâ™ ) is risky - you become a target
If you expose a card, you cannot play it when that suit is first led
The 10â™£ is dangerous - avoid taking it with other penalty cards
Sometimes taking all hearts is easier than avoiding them
Watch who leads - the pig holder from last game leads this game

engine.deckDescription: Standard 52-card deck comprising fifty-two cards: four suits of thirteen ranks each, with no jokers. Used for Gong Zhu (Chase the Lady) and similar games.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades), each with thirteen cards. Suits are equal in rank unless trumps apply.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit from Ace through King, Queen, Jack, down to 2. Standard ranking for trick-taking and shedding.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Chinese variation of Hearts featuring exposed penalty cards (doubling their values), special bonus cards, and the dramatic 'pig' role. Players aim to avoid reaching -1000 points while potentially executing all-hearts gambles for bonus points.
